text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Zajedno opposition coalition says it doubts in Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's intentions to recognize its victories in local elections.

- Milosevic in interview to Greek weekly says he is optimistic special law on recognition of election results will be passed, rejects all responsibility for war in Bosnia and for crisis in Serbia, which he blames on "external factors".
- New Democracy leadership denies rumours it will walk out of government.
- Serbian Radical Party leader Vojislav Seselj says radicals will not enter Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic's government.
- Serbian Orthodox Patriarch Pavle meets with top Bosnian Serb leadership, discusses negotiations on Brcko and relations between the church and the state.
- Yugoslav economists say independent experts' programme for radical reform good foundation for careful elaboration, especially of methods of privatisation and social policy.
- After announcement on abolition of ministry for private enterprise, private businessmen also announce street protests.
- Teachers in Serbia, whose strike over late wages and deteriorating conditions enters fourth week, say they will not give up as they are so impoverished they have nothing to lose.
POLITIKA
- Power should go to those who won it in elections, says Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic in interview to Greek weekly To Vima.
- In commentary on Zajedno coalition leaders' recent visit to Paris, Radio Belgrade describes French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette's conduct as "undiplomatic".
- Serbian energy and mining minister Dragan Kostic announces big changes at the helm of Serbian electric power industry.
- Yugoslav trade ministry announces further liberalisation of trade, free exports of consumer goods.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Belgrade districts Mladenovac and Novi Beograd, which Zajedno will try to include among the amendments on the Serbian parliament's agenda on Tuesday, were not disputed and are not on the OSCE report on local election results in Serbia.
- Serbs in Borovo Selo in eastern Slavonia region in Croatia on the verge of a mass exodus before the region's handover to Croatian authority, demand more safety guarantees.
- Ljiljana Milosavljevic, assistant Serbian Labour Minister, in response to criticism of new republican labour law, says it does not give managers unlimited powers.

- ICN Yugoslavia warns of manipulation with medicines, says local "centres of power" and speculators from abroad creating crisis to which immediate reaction is imports of medicines of poorer quality than those produced locally.
- Bar association of Belgrade says special law on election results unconstitutional. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
